items.text: WTI down 5.3% and Brent down 1.2% week-over-week as global growth concerns ease demand. With oil now off its highs despite Middle East tensions, energy-intensive credit (utilities, transporters, chemicals) faces less margin pressure, reducing refinancing risk in energy-linked covenant baskets.

Claims fell to 189K (down from 202K); unemployment at 4.1%, AHE growth modest at 3.12% YoY. Labor market loosening gradually but not in freefall—spreads reflect acceptance of a "no hard landing" narrative, though watch for any sharp claims spike signaling stress in lower-credit-quality sectors.

Headline CPI at 3.72% and PCE at 3.84% (data through Sept/Oct) remain sticky above target; PPI elevated at 6.52% YoY. Core PCE at 3.26% signals disinflationary services lag. This backdrop justifies the Fed's 4.0% rate hold and ECB's 2.50% deposit rate with 93% market pricing for a Dec 17 hike—credit remains in a "higher for longer" regime.

Fed paused at 4.0%; UST curve flattened to 25bp (2–10y) from 29bp, signaling inverted-rate-expectations volatility. ECB is 93% priced for a 25bp hike in December with 59bp of tightening forecast over 12 months. For special situations, watch cross-currency basis and refinancing windows in EUR-funding issuers; IG spreads at ~100bp OAS show complacency.

HY OAS at 377bp, up 14bp week-over-week; CCC OAS widened sharply to 1417bp (+30bp). This widening in lower-quality credit amid stable IG is classic distress signal—BBB/BB cliff refinancing risk rising. VIX at 26.8 (down from 28.4) suggests market volatility easing, but spread term structure remains steep.

GDPNow tracker fell to 2.90% (from 3.27% prior) amid retail weakness and consumer uncertainty. Payrolls showed +165K in Oct (+105K above prior), signaling resilience, but retail sales growth at 8.14% YoY is likely inflated by mix shift to autos. Housing starts at 1309K and existing home sales at 3.75M (lowest since 2010) signal demand destruction in real estate.

Michigan sentiment recovered to 51.5 final (Nov) from 48.0 (Oct), a post-election bounce, but households remain deeply depressed at ~1st percentile historicals. Housing crisis deepening: 30-year mortgage at 7.21% caps affordability; existing sales fell 5.5% MoM and 8.8% YoY. Rising cash-only deals (29% of sales) signal replacement of traditional debt financing—major credit underwriting cliff for mortgages & servicers.

themeCards.title: Housing Market Demand Collapse
themeCards.statusLine: Existing home sales hit 16-year low of 3.75M in October; 7.21% mortgage rates and affordability crisis driving cash deals to 29% of sales. First-time buyer share fell to 29% from 32% YoY.
themeCards.relevance: Existential refinancing risk for mortgage servicers, lenders, and mortgage REITs; rising default rates in jumbo/portfolio segments. HPA slowdown may force covenant breaches in CRE linked to transaction volume; refi walls loom for 2027–28 as ARM resets hit.

themeCards.title: CCC Credit & IG Spread Widening
themeCards.statusLine: CCC OAS at 1417bp (+30bp this week); HY OAS at 377bp suggests lower-quality issuers facing funding stress. Curve inversion and Fed hold at 4.0% reducing appeal of duration risk.
themeCards.relevance: Distressed debt opportunities in subordinated/junior cap structures; watch for covenant waivers, amendment fees, and loan-to-value resets. BBB/BB wall refinancing window closing; classic entry point for special situations investors hunting asymmetric risk/reward.

themeCards.title: ECB Tightening & EUR Basis Risk
themeCards.statusLine: ECB deposit rate at 2.50% with 93% odds of 25bp hike Dec 17; 59bp of tightening priced over 12 months. Euro inflation at 4.0%, double the 2% target; Eurozone PMI weakness signals growth risk.
themeCards.relevance: Cross-currency basis tightening; USD-funded EUR issuers facing higher swap costs and roll refinancing risk. BBB/BB European corporates may face downgrade pressure if growth stalls; special situations in subordinated EUR paper with covenant flexibility attractive.

themeCards.title: China Manufacturing Contraction & Trade Shock
themeCards.statusLine: Official manufacturing PMI forecast at 49.4 for November (yet to release), second month of contraction. Weak domestic demand, elevated input costs (Middle East energy), trade tensions mounting; export-driven growth model straining.
themeCards.relevance: Risk on global supply chain finance and trade-linked debt; Chinese dollar issuers face refinancing headwinds if growth outlook deteriorates further. Spillover to EM credit if China devaluation or stimulus expectations shift. Watch Hong Kong dollar soft-peg and yuan weakness implications for onshore/offshore spreads.

themeCards.title: GDPNow Momentum Fade & Payroll Noise
themeCards.statusLine: GDPNow tracker fell to 2.90% from 3.27%; retail ex-autos at 8.14% YoY looks inflated by mix shift. October payrolls +165K but prior revised down; labor market gradually softening without cliff risk.
themeCards.relevance: Consensus expects late-cycle slowdown without recession—favorable for BB/B credit outperformance but risky for CCC. If Q4 GDP comes in sub-2.0%, refinancing risk spikes and spread term premium widens; opportune entry for high-conviction distressed plays.

ecb.delta: On hold, 93% priced for +25bp Dec hike amid 4% euro inflation

chinaPMI.delta: Forecast Nov (yet to release); second month of contraction; weak domestic demand, elevated energy costs

ismServices.delta: October actual 54.5 (missed 54.8 consensus); Employment into expansion at 50.1

retailSales.delta: October data; ex-autos only; m/m data not in latest FRED snapshot

existingHome.delta: October SAAR; down 5.5% MoM, down 8.8% YoY; lowest since 2010

regime.label: Late-cycle slowdown
regime.detail: Fed on hold at 4%, ECB tightening into growth headwinds, spreads widening in lower quality, housing collapse, China weak—risk/reward tilts to high-conviction special situations and covenant-light lenders.
